doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Why Dizzy chose him: bebop with Afro-Cuban elements
summary: Mario Bauza recommended him to Dizzy, who wanted to fuse Afro-Cuban rhythms with jazz.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: It seems like you were the perfect choice for Dizzy Gillespie. I mean here he is a bebop innovator with an intense love of Cuban music and here you are, someone who can do both.

Well yes. I think that, I’m sure that was the key. This was a guy that was always looking for new things. He was the guy that, by the suggestion of the great Cuban musician Mario Bauza, he hired [gap] 39:25 so he saw something in me obviously, that showed us [gap] he saw a guy that had the potential of becoming a bebop jazz drummer bring to that style, to that genre all the Afro-Cuban elements that he loved. So I think I was the perfect [gap] for what he had in mind rhythmically speaking about fusioning Afro-Cuban rhythms with jazz. And the reason why that happened was because Mario Bauza was the one who saw me playing and recommended it to him. Dizzy didn’t see me playing nowhere. Mario Bauza saw me playing and called him up and told him about me.
